### math/vec3.js
Minimal vec3 utilities. All functions return new arrays, no mutation.

Exports: create, add, subtract, scale, dot, cross, length, normalize

Type: Vec3 = [number, number, number]

### math/vec2.js
Minimal vec2 utilities. All functions return new arrays, no mutation.

Exports: create, add, subtract, scale, dot, cross, perp, length, normalize

Type: Vec2 = [number, number]

Signatures of note:
- cross(a, b) -> number -- the z of the 3D cross product (signed parallelogram area). Positive when b is counter-clockwise from a.
- perp(v) -> Vec2 -- a quarter turn counter-clockwise, orthogonal to v and the same length.

### math/vec4.js
Minimal vec4 utilities. All functions return new arrays, no mutation.

Exports: create, add, subtract, scale, dot, length, normalize, fromVec3, toVec3, project

Type: Vec4 = [number, number, number, number]

Signatures of note:
- fromVec3(v, w=1) -> Vec4 -- w defaults to 1 (a point). Pass 0 for a direction.
- toVec3(v) -> Vec3 -- drops w. A truncation, never a perspective divide.
- project(v) -> Vec3 -- divides by w. w = 0 passes through unchanged, because that is a direction.

### math/vecn.js
Arbitrary-dimension vector utilities for a data-driven dimension (a feature vector, a coefficient list, a least-squares row). All functions return new arrays, no mutation. Prefer vec2/vec3/vec4 at a fixed dimension. Every binary operation REQUIRES equal lengths and throws a RangeError otherwise, so a wiring mistake never becomes a plausible number.

Exports: create, clone, add, subtract, multiply, scale, negate, dot, length, lengthSq, distance, normalize, lerp, sum, mean

Type: VecN = number[]

Signatures of note:
- create(n, fill=0) -> VecN -- throws on a negative or fractional n.
- multiply(a, b) -> VecN -- componentwise (Hadamard) product.
- normalize(v) -> VecN -- a zero vector stays zero (the length falls back to 1).
- lerp(a, b, t) -> VecN -- a t outside [0,1] extrapolates rather than clamping.
- mean(vectors) -> VecN -- componentwise mean of a list. Throws on an empty list.

### math/least-squares.js
Least-squares fitting. Pure, no DOM/GPU. The LINEAR solvers minimise the residual of A x = b, where each row is one equation. The GEOMETRIC fits minimise the ORTHOGONAL distance to a line, a plane or a circle. A y-on-x line fit tips over as the line turns vertical. An orthogonal fit does not. A singular system returns null, never a vector of NaN.

Types:

```ts
Matrix = readonly (readonly number[])[];  // row-major, equal-length rows
LineFit2 = { slope, intercept, rms };
OrthoLineFit2 = { point: Vec2; direction: Vec2; rms };
OrthoLineFit3 = { point: Vec3; direction: Vec3; rms };
PlaneFit = { point: Vec3; normal: Vec3; rms };
CircleFit2 = { center: Vec2; radius, rms };
Eigen3 = { values: [number,number,number]; vectors: [Vec3,Vec3,Vec3] };
Covariance3 = { mean: Vec3; matrix: number[][] };
```

Exports:
- solveLinear(a, b) -> number[] | null -- square solve, Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting. Null when singular.
- transpose(a) -> number[][], matVec(a, x) -> number[] -- the matrix helpers the fits use.
- solveLeastSquares(a, b, ridge=0) -> number[] | null -- normal equations (A^T A + ridge I) x = A^T b. A small ridge makes a rank-deficient system solvable, at the cost of bias.
- residuals(a, x, b) -> number[], rms(values) -> number -- rms of an empty vector is 0.
- evalPolynomial(coeffs, x) -> number -- coefficients in ASCENDING power order.
- fitPolynomial(xs, ys, degree) -> number[] | null -- ascending coefficients. The x values are centred and scaled internally, so x far from the origin still fits.
- fitLine(xs, ys) -> LineFit2 | null -- ordinary y-on-x fit. Null on vertical data.
- fitOrthoLine2(points) -> OrthoLineFit2 | null -- total least squares: minimises the perpendicular distance, so a vertical line is fine.
- fitCircle2(points) -> CircleFit2 | null -- algebraic (Kasa) fit through one linear solve. The rms reported is the TRUE geometric residual, not the algebraic one. Null for collinear points.
- covariance3(points) -> Covariance3 -- mean and the 3x3 covariance (divided by the count).
- symmetricEigen3(matrix) -> Eigen3 -- Jacobi rotations on a symmetric 3x3. Eigenvalues ASCENDING with matching orthonormal eigenvectors, each signed so its largest component is positive (deterministic, never an arbitrary flip).
- fitPlane(points) -> PlaneFit | null -- normal is the smallest-eigenvalue direction, through the centroid. Null for collinear points.
- fitOrthoLine3(points) -> OrthoLineFit3 | null -- direction is the largest-eigenvalue direction. The rms is the orthogonal point-to-line distance.

### math/cylinder-fit.js
Least-squares infinite-cylinder fit to a 3D point cloud (Eberly's formulation), minimising mean((|P(X-C)|^2 - r^2)^2). For a FIXED axis the centre and radius have a closed form, so the fit reduces to a search over directions. The search is a deterministic Hammersley hemisphere sweep (W and -W are the same cylinder) plus a local pattern search. The sweep is what handles a SHORT wide cylinder. That cloud is flat, so its principal axis is perpendicular to the true axis, and a local-only search fails there.

Types:

```ts
CylinderFit = { center: Vec3; axis: Vec3; radius, error, rms, height, extent: [number,number] };
CylinderFitOptions = { direction?: Vec3; directionSamples?: number; refineSteps?: number; tolerance?: number };
```

Exports:
- fitCylinder(points, options?) -> CylinderFit | null -- sweep plus refinement. Null below five points, which is how many degrees of freedom a cylinder has. Options: direction (an initial axis guess, which SKIPS the sweep), directionSamples (default 256), refineSteps (default 64), tolerance (default 1e-9).
- fitCylinderForAxis(points, direction) -> CylinderFit | null -- the closed form for a KNOWN axis, plus the energy that axis achieves. The direction need not be a unit vector. Null when every point lies on the axis.
- distanceToCylinderSurface(fit, p) -> number -- signed distance to the fitted surface, negative inside. The caps are not considered.

On the CylinderFit result:
- center -- the axis point nearest the centroid.
- axis -- the unit direction. A cylinder fixes it only up to sign.
- radius, rms -- the fitted radius, and the radial residual |P(X-C)| - r in point units.
- error -- Eberly's energy. This is the number that compares one fit against another.
- height, extent -- how far the DATA reaches along the infinite axis.

### math/mat4.js
Minimal mat4 utilities. Column-major Float32Array(16). Imports vec3 internally.

Exports: create, identity, perspective, perspectiveGL, lookAt, multiply, translate, rotateX, rotateY, rotateZ, scale, reflectY, reflectZ, transpose, normalMatrix, normalMatrix3, invert

Type: Mat4 = Float32Array

Signatures of note:
- perspective(fovY, aspect, near, far) -> Mat4 -- WebGPU clip-Z [0,1].
- perspectiveGL(fovY, aspect, near, far) -> Mat4 -- OpenGL/WebGL clip-Z [-1,1] (use for a WebGL2 pipeline. Contrast perspective above).
- rotateZ(m, angle) -> Mat4 -- rotate about Z (mirrors rotateX/rotateY).
- transpose(m) -> Mat4 -- 4x4 transpose.
- normalMatrix(m) -> Mat4 -- transpose-of-inverse of the upper 3x3, embedded in a 4x4 (returns identity() if singular).
- normalMatrix3(m) -> Float32Array(9) -- the same transform as a column-major mat3 (the GLSL/WGSL normal-matrix form). Returns the identity 3x3 if singular (matching normalMatrix).

### math/sdf.js
Pure signed-distance-field math (no DOM/GPU): primitives, a column-major point transform, a CPU grid bake of an arbitrary scene SDF. Also trilinear sampling with a continuous outside-the-box extension, ray/AABB intersection, and the Inigo Quilez closest-approach soft-shadow march. Mirror these formulas in any WGSL/GLSL twin.

Constants: SDF_SPHERE, SDF_BOX, SDF_CYLINDER, SDF_TORUS

Types:

```ts
SdfParams = readonly [number,number,number,number];
SdfGrid = { data: Float32Array; dims: [number,number,number]; volMin: Vec3; volMax: Vec3 };
SceneSDF = (x,y,z) => number;
SdfAabb = { min: Vec3; max: Vec3 };
SoftShadowOptions, SoftShadowResult = { vis: number; steps: number };
```

Exports:
- sdSphere(p, [radius]), sdBox(p, [hx,hy,hz]), sdCylinder(p, [radius,halfH]), sdTorus(p, [majorR,minorR]) -> number -- local-space primitive distances (Vec3 p).
- primitiveSDF(type, p, params) -> number -- dispatch a primitive by SDF_* id.
- transformPoint(m, p) -> Vec3 -- column-major affine point transform (w=1).
- makeGrid(scene, volMin, volMax, dims) -> SdfGrid -- one-time CPU bake of a scene callback `scene(x,y,z) => distance` into a dense voxel-centre grid.
- trilinear(grid, q) -> number -- trilinear fetch at a clamped [0,1] coordinate.
- sampleGrid(grid, p) -> number -- sample at a world point. Inside = trilinear, outside = max(edgeValue, distanceToBox) (continuous, never falsely shadowed).
- intersectAABB(ro, rd, bmin, bmax) -> [tNear, tFar] (ray misses when tFar < max(tNear,0)).
- softShadow(sampleFn, ro, rd, opts?) -> { vis, steps } -- IQ soft visibility in [0,1]. Opts: { tmin, tmax, k, maxSteps, minStep, maxStep, eps, aabb }.

### math/noise.js
Deterministic procedural noise -- integer hash -> value noise -> fbm, 2D and 3D. Pure. Outputs in [0,1] unless noted. The 2D lattice is tileable (the hash wraps by `cells`). The 3D lattice is unbounded.

Exports:
- hash2(ix, iy, period, seed) -> [0,1) -- tileable 2D lattice hash.
- smootherstep(t) -> number -- quintic easing 6t^5-15t^4+10t^3.
- valueNoise2(u, v, cells, seed) -> [0,1) -- tileable 2D value noise.
- fbm2(u, v, baseCells, octaves, seed) -> [0,1) -- 2D fractal Brownian motion.
- ridged2(u, v, baseCells, octaves, seed) -> [0,1) -- (1-|2*fbm-1|)^2 ridges.
- hash3(x, y, z, seed) -> [0,1) -- 3D lattice hash (non-tiling).
- valueNoise3(x, y, z, seed) -> [0,1) -- 3D value noise.
- fbm3(x, y, z, seed, octaves=4) -> [0,1) -- 3D fractal Brownian motion.

### math/sampling.js
Low-discrepancy + hemisphere sampling. Pure, deterministic. radicalInverse2 / hammersley match the GPU convention in webgpu/shaders/prefilter.wgsl, so the same index yields the same point on CPU and GPU.

Exports:
- radicalInverse2(i) -> [0,1) -- van der Corput base 2 (radicalInverse2(0)=0).
- hammersley(i, n) -> [number, number] -- [i/n, radicalInverse2(i)] (hammersley(0,n)=[0,0]).
- uniformHemisphere(u, v) -> Vec3 -- uniform-solid-angle direction on +Z (u=costheta).
- cosineHemisphere(u, v) -> Vec3 -- cosine-weighted direction on +Z (Malley, r=sqrt(u)).

### math/gaussian-kernel.js
Separable Gaussian blur kernel builder (linear-sampling). Pure math. Merges adjacent tap pairs into one bilinear fetch at a fractional texel offset (halves the texture samples while reproducing the exact discrete Gaussian).

Type: GaussianKernel = { sigma, radius, weights: number[], entries: [offset,weight][] }

Exports:
- MAX_RADIUS: number -- kernel-radius cap (192).
- buildGaussianKernel(sigma) -> GaussianKernel -- entries[0] is the centre tap. Entries[1..] are side taps sampled at BOTH +offset and -offset. Two-sided integer-tap weights sum to exactly 1.
